target_customer: Single-operator microbusinesses and small shops in Latin America, such as tiendas, bakeries, salons and restaurants
problem: About 90 percent of Latin America's roughly 50 million microbusinesses record sales and debts on paper, so they lack a view of their finances and cannot access credit.
business_model: Freemium mobile ledger and inventory app with paid monthly plans (Essential and Pro), expanding into payments and financial products
product_category: Microbusiness bookkeeping, inventory and POS app, later AI tools

founders.name: Lluis Canadell
founders.background_notes: Background not found in sources opened; TechCrunch 2021 and the YC page give none.

founders.name: Man Hei Lou
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; background not found.

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile bookkeeping and inventory app is standard engineering; the hard parts were scale, offline use and later payments and credit.

defensibility.rationale: Ledgers and transaction history lock in merchants and create data for credit, but similar apps are easy to build.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent buying or copying is documented in sources read; Bold and SumUp are cited in 2020s listings as payment rivals.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (2021-02) reported monthly users up 400 percent since the August 2020 launch, 35,000 monthly active users in January 2021 and over 25 million dollars in gross transaction volume, with most Latin American microbusinesses still on paper.

branding.domain_note: Uses treinta.co, a .co domain; no history found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain Spanish product copy aimed at shopkeepers; testimonials from bakeries, hardware and beauty shops

branding.community_and_virality: Forbes Colombia described the app as viral in 2022; the company reports an app rating of 4.8 on its site.

brand_strength.rationale: A short Spanish word (thirty) with good recall in Colombia and viral growth cited by press, but no evidence the name drove growth.

outcome_analysis: Treinta launched in August 2020, reached tens of thousands of monthly users within months, raised a 46 million Series A in April 2022 and claims millions of businesses. A 2026 profile says it later shrank to a smaller team focused on its management software after other products were dropped. It is active, with a reported 30,000 paying customers.
notes: Series A lead conflicts across sources (Luxor Capital and PayU in one, PayU with Prosus, Liontree and others in another); the Gunder page names none. The 14.3M figure of June 2021 is from a Forbes Colombia headline linked on the YC page; the article body and stage were not opened, so stage is other and investors are unknown. Total funding stated as 60M in one source. A search summary says the name refers to saving users 30 minutes a day; not sourced to a page I opened, so name_origin is null. Competition at founding: TechCrunch (2021-02) names no competitors and no dated rival source was found; later lists name Bold, SumUp, Alegra and ContaAzul but not dated to founding. The 2026 downsizing detail comes from a Growth.Talent summary snippet only.
